stories.title: At least 16 dead, 28 injured, in Egypt bus crash
stories.summary: Bus crashes on Dahab-Nuweiba road on the eastern coast of the Sinai Peninsula, an area popular with tourists. A bus crash in Egypt’s South Sinai governorate has killed 16 people and injured 28 others, the Ministry of Health and Population said. The incident happened on Wednesday morning on the road from Dahab to Nuweiba on the eastern coast of the Sinai Peninsula, an area with resorts along the Red Sea popular with tourists. Health Ministry spokesman Hossam Abdel Ghaffar said 20 ambulances were dispatched to the scene to evacuate and treat the wounded. Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar ordered medical facilities to raise their level of preparedness and provide the injured with necessary medical care, medicines and supplies. Deadly road accidents are common in Egypt. Last year, nearly 6,000 people died in road accidents across the country, according to Egypt’s state statistics agency. Last month, 18 people were killed and 30 injured in a road accident in the northeastern governorate of Ismailia.

stories.summary: In the 46th episode of Health Wrap by The Hindu, Health Editor Ramya Kannan and Senior Assistant Editor Zubeda Hamid discuss some of the key health stories in focus this week. The episode looks at changes in childhood vaccination policy in the U.S., newer approaches to TB diagnosis and multi-testing, the gender gap in cancer care and what Okinawa’s Blue Zone can tell us about longevity and healthy ageing.

stories.title: Fire-walking during Aadi festivals: How to escape burns?Health Wrap | Episode 48
stories.summary: Aadi, the Tamil month associated with several temple festivals and religious observances, sees many devotees taking part in practices such as fire-walking and prolonged barefoot walking. Exposure to extreme heat can cause burns, blisters and other injuries to the feet. In this episode of Health Wrap, Ramya Kannan, Health Editor, The Hindu, speaks to an expert about the risks of foot injuries during fire-walking, what people should watch out for after exposure to extreme heat and when an injury requires medical attention.
